# World processes integration recipe

## Canonical skill routing (do not invent a second index)

The authoritative repository catalog is `skills/catalog.json`,
**generated by** `tools/skills/catalog.py` (not a manually maintained
INDEX.md). The ten dedicated capability-specific skills are:

| Need | Open only this skill |
|---|---|
| ECHO hearing/portals | `skills/world/aiverse-echo/SKILL.md` |
| FRACTURE supports/collapse | `skills/world/aiverse-fracture/SKILL.md` |
| AETHER smoke/gas ducts | `skills/world/aiverse-aether/SKILL.md` |
| MORPH deformation/impacts | `skills/world/aiverse-morph/SKILL.md` |
| CROWD route/slots | `skills/world/aiverse-crowd/SKILL.md` |
| IMPRINT footprints/scent | `skills/world/aiverse-imprint/SKILL.md` |
| CIRCUIT electricity/devices | `skills/world/aiverse-circuit/SKILL.md` |
| GRANULAR loose solids/terrain | `skills/world/aiverse-granular/SKILL.md` |
| EVOLVE region/forest ecology | `skills/world/aiverse-evolve/SKILL.md` |
| SOCIETY knowledge/NPC events | `skills/world/aiverse-society/SKILL.md` |

Prefer routing through `python3 tools/skills/catalog.py search "query"`
or `python3 tools/skills/catalog.py plan --skills aiverse-morph --side both`.
The shared `aiverse-world-processes` recipe only coordinates multiple
mechanisms. Each specialized skill has a stable catalog ID, precise
C++20 API/owner contract, native CMake opt-in path and a handoff index.
There are no per-genre skill variants and no invented per-skill
CMake library targets. New gameplay systems and Studio assets remain
source-only until native tests and visual QA are actually run.


Read `AGENTS.md`, `docs/agents/ecs.md`, `docs/ecs-mechanic-composition.md`, and `docs/handoffs/world-processes-stage01-2026-11-23.md`.

Ten policy experiments live in `libraries/include/aiverselib/world/WorldProcesses.h`:
- `supported` (FRACTURE), `diffuse` (AETHER), `relax` (MORPH), `audibility` (ECHO), `assignSlots` (CROWD),
  `erode` (IMPRINT), `energize` (CIRCUIT), `settle` (GRANULAR), `age` (EVOLVE), `shareKnowledge` (SOCIETY).

These functions do not touch `Simulation`. They are intentionally NOT self-contained game mechanics. Integrate only the chosen process:
1. Search the owners' existing components and source first; extend shared engine capability rather than reimplementing it.
2. Define data-only component contracts, deterministic unit/scale, validation, stable schema ID, `io` persistence, explicit read/write stage and event barrier.
3. Use integer/fixed authoritative state only. Do not write hidden mutable arrays or genre modes. Keep presentation decoupled.
4. Implement native consumers and verify test coverage for deterministic ordering, invalid indexes, boundaries, save/load, rollback/replay and different worker counts.
5. For anything seen in the editor, add generic component metadata and a minimal website demo with genuine frames when it becomes a usable capability.
6. Document actual verification; never claim the provisional pure-policy probes are shipped ECS features.
7. At the end of each stage, update the handoff (branch, SHA, changed files, API, tests run, limitations and exact next action). Respect the five-area WIP limit and main-merge gate.

Smoke test: `bash tests/libraries/world_processes_run.sh`.


## Stage 02: ECHO's first ECS integration
`libraries/include/aiverselib/world/EchoEcs.h` is the reusable, opt-in gameplay hearing pass. Call `aiverse::echo::install(sim)` once inside the native `GameModule::setup`; create `AcousticZone`, `AcousticPortal`, `AcousticEmitter`, `AcousticReceiver`, and `AcousticHearing` components on entities. Source, zone and portal references use generation-safe ECS `Entity` handles. The system publishes authoritative `AcousticHearing`; do not create a parallel AI perception cache. A host can instead call `propagate(world,tick)` explicitly at its read/write barrier.

The native test is `ecs_echo_acoustics_test` (source `tests/ecs_echo_acoustics_test.cpp`). It covers COW rollback, save/reload, deterministic graph tie ordering, stale refs and bounded oversized inputs, but **has not been executed or validated on the current branch yet**. Run on a real build before calling the feature verified. ECHO currently models authored zone portals, not full audio ray tracing or reverb. See `docs/handoffs/world-processes-stage02-echo-2026-11-23.md`.

## Stage 03: FRACTURE structural ECS

Public headers: `aiverselib/world/FractureEcs.h` (always) and `aiverselib/world/FracturePhysisBridge.h` (optional PHYSIS integration). Use the **existing** PHYSIS nature stress/outbox and host's Box3D/TerraWeave physics; never recalculate wind/fire/quake stress or spawn physics inside FRACTURE.

In `GameModule::setup`, call `fracture::install(sim)` after any PHYSIS installer. Place `fracture::Member` on each structural part Entity, `fracture::Bond` on each link Entity; attach `fracture::Collapse` to parts whose physical detachment needs durable dispatch. Provide one or more anchored members. A damage-capability/authorized command changes `Member.broken` or `Bond.damage`; `fracture::advance(world,tick)` marks unsupported members detached and emits one pending collapse transition. Call `fracture::pending(world)`, stage/deduplicate the actual gameplay/Box3D/TerraWeave effect **durably**, then `fracture::acknowledge(world,event)`. Only a trusted repair should call `rearmAfterRepair` after the original event is acknowledged, original tick has passed, and bonds/physics are repaired.

PHYSIS hookup: call `addPhysisFractureBridgeSystem(sim)` **after** `physis.nature_stress` and **before** registering `fracture.support`. It reads `physis::NatureStressOutputComponent` and latches Member.broken; PHYSIS remains the source of environmental fracture facts. Do not attach a duplicate Collapse outbox to the PHYSIS primary fall event's body; let the PHYSIS durable outbox handle that object's falling reaction, and use Collapse for downstream structural members. The host reconciles the single physical-effects ledger.

Native regression: `ecs_fracture_structure_test` from `tests/ecs_fracture_structure_test.cpp` (CTest), including support cascade, damaged bonds, PHYSIS snapshot bridge, event ack/rearm, COW replay, save/load and stale Entity generation. Newly added code has **not passed a full native build or CI acceptance gate** yet; never mark ready just from presence of tests. Stage handoff: `docs/handoffs/world-processes-stage03-fracture-2026-11-23.md`.

## Stage 04: AETHER gas diffusion (experimental ECS integration)

Public interfaces: `aiverselib/world/AetherEcs.h`, optional `aiverselib/world/AetherPhysisBridge.h`. To enable, call `aiverse::aether::install(sim)` during native `GameModule::setup`, then attach `GasCell` to ECS room/volume/cell entities, `GasDuct` to ventilation/link entities and optional `GasFlux` to sources or sinks. These are **gas species only**: PHYSIS retains weather, climate, wind and fire. Equal-volume cells use integer-quantized masses of `smoke`, `toxin`, `oxygen`; a duct implements concentration-driven diffusion with a maximum mass transfer per tick, not a full computational-fluid-dynamics solver.

`aether::advance(world,tick)` stages all three species and fluxes before committing. The policy enforces signed rate/mass bounds and stable entity sorting, and refuses mixed partially-processed tick states. Call once per authoritative tick. State persists through registered `aether.gas_cell`, `aether.duct`, `aether.flux` v1 schemas.

To connect PHYSIS fire, call `aether::addPhysisFireSystem(sim)` after PHYSIS environment and after gas transport, during setup, when PHYSIS `State` and `HazardCell` exist. Attach `FireCoupling` to PHYSIS cell entities also containing `GasCell`. `applyPhysisFire(world)` reads current normalized fire intensity and creates smoke/consumes oxygen once per PHYSIS climate tick. It **does not extinguish or modify PHYSIS fire**; combustion chemistry, smoke light scattering and physical wind advection are not implemented. `FireCoupling` is a persistent opt-in `aether.fire_coupling` v1 component; do not register twice.

Acceptance source `tests/ecs_aether_gas_test.cpp` / CTest `ecs_aether_gas_test`: conservation, deterministic cross-module hashes, invalid flux fail-closed, duplicate tick, stale generations, PHYSIS coupling, COW save/replay. Tests were authored, **not verified as compiled/passed** in this session. Handoff: `docs/handoffs/world-processes-stage04-aether-2026-11-23.md`. Follow the five-area WIP limit and do not enable 4th+ system before closing current ECHO/FRACTURE/AETHER gates.

## Stage 07: bounded Studio map authoring with real Undo/Redo

The approved Studio Scene Inspector uses `StudioSession::componentCatalog`,
`studio.componentAdd`, `studio.componentRemove`, and
`studio.setProperty` / `studio.setProperties`. MapDoc supplies
single-step Undo/Redo and project serialization. The new pure, validated
`libraries/include/aiverselib/world/WorldProcessesAuthoring.h` can author
only three self-contained components initially:

- `EchoZone`: `enabled` boolean.
- `FractureMember`: `anchored` boolean. Runtime `broken`/`detached`
  are simulation state and MUST NOT be editable as authoring data.
- `AetherGasCell`: integer initial `smoke`, `toxin`, `oxygen`
  (0..1,000,000,000), `enabled` boolean. `sampledTick` is a runtime value.

Editing requires `components[ComponentId]` in real map DocEntity extras,
and fails closed on wrong types, unknown keys, partial schemas, fractional
or out-of-range numeric values. `StudioSessionTests` tests add/edit,
batch rollback, Undo, Redo, save and reload.

**Critical:** Editor authoring DOES NOT automatically install
world-process ECS components into existing game modules. A native game's
entity-spawn step must map its stable authored document ID to a
generation-safe ECS Entity, then call
`lib::worldprocess::authoring::apply(world, entity, componentId, json)`
before registering/stepping the ECHO/FRACTURE/AETHER systems. This is
explicitly opt-in and returns false on invalid data or duplicate
components. The Live Inspector remains read-only. Do not claim
end-to-end gameplay authoring until a concrete game module consumes
these extras and a real scene verifies it.

Tests: `world_processes_authoring_test` in focused CI plus the
native `apps/studio-native/tests/StudioSessionTests.cpp` fixture
and CMake/Studio test targets. Source added does not prove CI green
until real logs are recorded. Follow handoff
`docs/handoffs/world-processes-stage07-authoring-2026-11-23.md`.

## Stage 08: real map-to-native ECS hydration

Use `aiverselib/world/WorldProcessesMapHydration.h`:
`authoring::hydrateMap(Simulation&, map, placedEntities)` inside an owning
native `GameModule::setup` **after map Entity creation** and before the
persistence registry seals. The `placedEntities` vector is the host's
exact index-order mapping of `map["entities"]` to actual generation-safe
ECS Entity handles. A mismatched count, dead/unspawned Entity, invalid
value or budget exceed fails before registration/mutation. Only categories
actually present are registered; a map without World Processes leaves the
legacy v9 schema alone.

For the existing GameCore host use the standard native module adapter
`aiverselib/world/WorldProcessesNativeModule.h`. The native module's
`setup(GameCore&,Simulation&,NativeState&,Json)` reads
`host.matchMap()` (post-generation map) and `host.mapPlaced()`.
It is invoked at the established `NativeModules::load` lifecycle. No
modification to engine/GameCore sources or second simulation is required.

**Ready-to-copy CMake/project template**:
`examples/native/world_processes/`. Register
`aiverse_native_module(ID world_processes VERSION 1 ENTRY
createWorldProcessesModule SOURCES WorldProcessesModule.cpp)`, link the
native OBJECT target to `AIVERSE::libraries`, and enable
`{"id":"world_processes"}` in the project `rules.json`
`nativeModules` list. This is explicitly opt-in, not automatic for
unmodified games. Built-in generic real-GameCore test:
`tests/world_processes_gamecore_native_test.cpp`; lightweight
two-GameModule map/save/rollback test:
`tests/world_processes_map_hydration_test.cpp`.
They are staged and **must be built/run before being reported green**.

Current automatic hydration supports only three standalone editor-authorable
types: EchoZone, FractureMember, AetherGasCell. Generational links to ECHO
Portal/Receiver/Emitter, FRACTURE Bond, AETHER Duct/Flux require a separate
validated map-ref resolution stage and a Studio picker. No numeric index
fallback. See
`docs/handoffs/world-processes-stage08-native-hydration-2026-11-23.md`.

## Stage 09: stable map-object connections (ECHO, FRACTURE, AETHER)

Shared C++ validation/adapter:
`aiverselib/world/WorldProcessesLinkedAuthoring.h`. Linked authored
components with stable **map document IDs**, NOT numeric `Entity.index`:
`EchoPortal(from,to,loss,bidirectional,enabled)`,
`EchoEmitter(zone,intensity,enabled)`,
`EchoReceiver(zone,threshold,enabled)`,
`FractureBond(first,second,strength,damage,enabled)`,
`AetherDuct(from,to,maximumPerTick,oneWay,enabled)`,
`AetherFlux(cell,smoke,toxin,oxygen,enabled)`.
New configs start disabled and unbound. For enabled links, all required
targets must exist; two-ended links need distinct IDs. Numeric ranges and
types are validated with exact integer parsing. Do not expose runtime-only
`EchoHearing`, `FractureCollapse` or PHYSIS transient state as authoring.

`WorldProcessesMapHydration.h` does a deterministic two-phase map
preflight, checks unique stable IDs, live generation-safe ECS handle
mapping and compatible endpoint components, then hydrates standalone
components FIRST, linked components SECOND. The source of truth is still
one World; mapping is a transient setup-time lookup, not serialized.
Authored EchoReceiver automatically gets its authoritative
`AcousticHearing` output component.

HTML5 Studio: existing Inspector `componentCatalog/add/remove/setProperty/
setProperties` accepts linked types. Reference fields expose native-backed
options and the shared `EntityReferencePicker` (searchable object list,
drag from Hierarchy via `application/x-aiverse-entity`,
stable `entity:@id` values only). Native validates target ID and
required component on each write. A multi-field link paste is staged
atomically into one MapDoc Undo step. Referenced target components cannot
be removed until incoming links are cleared. Entity *deletion* and map-ID
renames still require a complete graph-aware authoring cleanup workflow;
game setup will reject stale IDs rather than silently rebind.

Tests: `tests/world_processes_linked_test.cpp` and extended
`apps/studio-native/tests/StudioSessionTests.cpp`, plus CMake/CI.
Until latest CI/native Mac builds and screenshots pass, label this stage
**source implemented, not verified**. Handoff:
`docs/handoffs/world-processes-stage09-linked-authoring-2026-11-23.md`.

## Stages 11–16: complete genre-neutral ECS core and opt-in Studio authoring

All ten initially requested world-process mechanic areas now have authored
native ECS source code: ECHO, FRACTURE, AETHER, MORPH, CROWD, IMPRINT,
CIRCUIT, GRANULAR, EVOLVE and SOCIETY. In addition to the earlier three,
the seven opt-in headers and their persistent v1 schemas are:

- `MorphEcs.h`: Node/Spring/Force (deformation and shape-memory constraints).
- `CrowdEcs.h`: Agent/Slot/Preference (deterministic placement/avoidance).
- `ImprintEcs.h`: Cell/Link/Deposit (footprints, scent and trace diffusion).
- `CircuitEcs.h`: Node/Wire/Gate (generator/load routing, AND/OR/XOR/NOT).
- `GranularEcs.h`: Field/Source (bounded 2D granular settling).
- `EvolveEcs.h`: Region/Pressure (time-dependent world succession).
- `SocietyEcs.h`: Person/Contact/Message (trusted information spread).

Every system has a bounded, deterministic `advance(World&,tick)`,
`registerPersistence(Simulation&)` and `install(Simulation&)`. Ownership
stays with existing world/physics/economy/narrative systems; these modules
do not create a second rigid-body, NavMesh, terrain, water, fire or UI engine.

`WorldProcessesSuite.h` provides strict boolean flags to install any
combination through the existing `world_processes` native module. The
`WorldProcessesExtendedAuthoring.h` and `WorldProcessesExtendedLinks.h`
schemas cover all 19 component types from the seven areas, including
generation-safe references to real project map objects. Map setup uses
`WorldProcessesMapHydration.h` to validate/resolve stable IDs, create the
real ECS pools and register schemas, not a JSON mirror of runtime state.

Studio now supports Add Component, typed parameter bounds, the searchable
map object picker, drag/drop from Hierarchy, atomic field changes and
MapDoc Undo/Redo for the seven systems as well as the original three.
`WorldProcessesExtendedInspector.h` appends read-only current ECS values to
the existing WorldInspect/Live Inspector route.

`GranularDocument.h` supports up to 128x128 2D maps, per-cell mass and
obstacles, resizing and brush painting; the Scene Inspector mounts the
shared-theme `GranularGridEditor.tsx`. One completed user paint action
commits one validated full-grid JSON document through the existing
`studio.setProperty({componentId:"GranularField",key:"grid",value:JSON})`
RPC. Native `GranularDocument::apply` creates real ECS field cells.
The simple 1x1 `initialMass/capacity` form remains backward compatible.

Game/audio/AI/render consumers should use
`WorldProcessesQueries.h` (`morphPose/morphPoses`, `crowdPose`,
`imprintLevels`, `circuitState`, `granularCell`, `evolution`,
`societyPerson/knowsTopic`) to read the one authoritative ECS World.
These read-only projections are not secondary physics/NPC state.

A full native template fragment of stable IDs and authored component data
for all seven mechanisms is available in
`examples/native/world_processes/authoring-examples.json`; merge its
components into a *real* project's map entities with valid entity types,
owners and positions. The normal opt-in native project example and
`rules.json` flags are documented in its README.

**Test policy:** The user explicitly deferred testing for these stages.
Do not claim the new headers/Studio components compile or pass CTest,
sanitizers, Mac GUI or merged-tree `./run-tests.sh --quick`: they have
not been verified yet. See the complete stage handoffs in
`docs/handoffs/world-processes-stage11-*-` through Stage16.
Functional limitations: graphical soft-body mesh skinning, actual
Box3D impact/collapse, global RVO/NavMesh, full SPH granular physics,
real sound HRTF, terrain re-meshing, and game-specific NPC social
behavior remain consuming integration responsibilities, not promises
fulfilled by the ECS policy layer.


## Stages 17–19: actual MORPH + GRANULAR Box3D / RHI / TerraWeave host

For optional physical 3D scenes, DO NOT import physics or renderer into the
genre-neutral libraries header layer. Use the native project integration in
examples/world/world_processes_native/ instead:

- MorphModelStream.h: real per-instance ModelVertex GPU stream override;
  supplies weighted ECS MorphNode vertex displacements through the existing
  Renderer3D ModelDraw on Metal/Vulkan/GLES backends. Set Model::batching.allowGeometryPool=false **before** model upload and retain the immutable
  source vertex/index arrays. Never overwrite shared global GPU geometry.
  The separate instance stream owns its buffers and must retire them at a
  completed Device idle/lifetime fence.
- MorphBox3DContactBridge.h: authoritative Box3D Scene begin contacts and
  body velocities to quantized integer MorphContactInput records. Only the
  authoritative host samples float physics; replay clients use recorded
  integer inputs. MORPH now owns morph::Impact, persistent version-1
  morph.impact, applied **once** at the intended ECS tick. Do not reuse the
  continuous MorphForce component for one-shot contacts.
- GranularTerraWeaveBinding.h: sample canonical granular::Field + the
  existing TerraWeave EarthworksLayer ground height, bake granular slabs
  into render::MeshBuilder and the matching Box3D static top collision
  surface. Each optional native publisher has its own revision and resource
  lifetime; a failed collider creation retains the previous ground.
- GranularWorldIntegration.h: choose complete physics+visible 16x16 grid
  tiles, prepare immutable chunks on a completed ECS/soil revision,
  publish on the Box3D owner thread between Scene::step calls and the
  graphics owner thread outside rendered frames. Gate simulation/render
  when any batch patch rejects; individual tile replacement is safe but
  full multi-tile publication is not one atomic cross-device transaction.
- GranularTerraWeaveTransfer.h: real Dig/Fill via the canonical
  TerraWeave ECS excavateAuthoritativeEcs operation. A host explicitly
  defines one granular mass unit = one cubic centimetre for this transfer,
  preflights the actual EarthworksLayer::sculpt movedVolumeCm3, checks
  capacity/mass, then credits/debits the one authoritative granular pool.
  Ground renderer, collider and NavMesh remain TerraWeave owner outputs,
  never mutated by the gameplay policy itself.
- PhysicalSceneHost.h: convenient native C++ facade for MORPH instance
  streams, recorded contacts, GRANULAR frame prepare/publish/draw,
  rollback invalidation and safe shutdown.
- Full lifecycle integration source code and dependency boundaries:
  examples/world/world_processes_native/README.md.

The adapters are **opt-in to the concrete native project** and must be
linked only when that project already owns a renderer/gfx Device, a Box3D
Scene and a TerraWeave authoritative World. The minimal
examples/native/world_processes/ module remains independent from Box3D.
A MORPH visual 3D shape is not automatically an exact deformable Box3D
collision shape; the optional kinematic proxy stays coarse. GRANULAR is
a bounded 2D projected loose-solid layer, not SPH fluid, per-grain rigid
bodies or a second terrain engine. None of these are default engine
system replacements.

The user explicitly requested tests later. **No CMake/CTest/ASan, backend
GPU frame, actual Box3D scene or Mac screenshot has been verified** for
Stages17–19; do not claim green. Every further stage must add its own

## Stages 20–21: CROWD NavMesh route + IMPRINT movement trackers

CROWD navigation:
`aiverselib/world/CrowdRoutes.h` adds persistent `crowd.route`
(`Route`, bounded quantized waypoints, cursor and navigation revision).
`crowd::assignRoute` receives an authoritative route, while
`crowd::advanceRoutes` selects the next waypoint ahead of the normal
`crowd::advance` local avoidance system. The optional native
`examples/world/world_processes_native/CrowdNavMeshBridge.h`
`planCrowdNavRoute` runs the EXISTING engine `nav::Mesh::findPath`
with real TerraWeave terrain heights, then converts Fixed metres into
integer centimetres once and stores the path in ECS. The NavMesh is
never cloned or updated by CROWD. A host re-plans following nav revisions.

IMPRINT trace generation:
`aiverselib/world/ImprintTrails.h` adds persistent
`imprint.tracker` (`Tracker`), authoritative `sampleMotion` and
`stampMotion`. A tracker records a source Entity and target
`ImprintCell` plus spacing, trace rates and last sampled positions.
`WorldProcessesSuite` runs `imprint.motion_trails` before IMPRINT
diffusion. If both CROWD and IMPRINT are enabled, the optional
`ImprintCrowdBridge.h` runs after CROWD movement and automatically
feeds CROWD agents to their trackers. Trackers whose source is a
non-CROWD Entity are left for their owning Box3D/ActorMotor game host
to call `imprint::sampleMotion` on the ECS tick barrier.

Studio Add Component supports `ImprintTracker`, with native-validated
stable map-ID source picker (ANY authored entity) and target cell picker
(only real `ImprintCell` components). Enabled link requires both IDs.
Normal MapDoc Undo/Redo, Save and reference-protected delete apply.
Live Inspector exposes read-only current `CrowdRoute` and
`ImprintTracker` ECS fields.

## Stages 22–25: CIRCUIT device actuation, EVOLVE ecology, SOCIETY NPC events

**CIRCUIT.** `CircuitDevices.h` adds the real persisted `Switch`
and `Device` ECS types, with `circuit.switch` /
`circuit.device` v1 schemas. `setSwitch` accepts authoritative
player/game input; `synchronizeSwitches` writes Node.drive only
where one unambiguous switch owns that input; `circuit.power_logic`
solves the original graph; `updateDevices` derives powered/signal
device output and monotonic transition counters. The suite order is
switch inputs -> logic solver -> device outputs. Switch/Device
stable-ID authoring, link resolution, budget validation, Studio
component picker and Live Inspector are implemented.
`examples/world/world_processes_native/CircuitDeviceHost.h` applies
configured door devices to **existing** Box3D kinematic bodies via
`Scene::moveKinematic`, and calls project-supplied handlers for light,
motors, pumps, alarms or other devices. The engine does not acquire
a second electrical or rigid-body authority.

**EVOLVE.** `EvolvePhysisBridge.h` defines persistable
`evolve::ClimateLink`, which reads **existing** PHYSIS Atmosphere and
Surface data and writes only a canonical EVOLVE Pressure ECS component
before the region evolution tick.
`examples/world/world_processes_native/EvolvePhysisHost.h` provides
`attachEvolveClimate` after actual source/region entities exist.
`EvolveTerraEcologyBridge.h` wraps the **existing**
`TerraWeaveForestEcology.h` ForestEcologyClimateSampler to limit
nutrient and light according to EVOLVE fertility/succession/pollution,
without overwriting the PHYSIS/NEREID baseline or TerraWeave plant
registry. The host decides region world bounds and synchronizes its
ecology phase after completed EVOLVE tick.

**SOCIETY.** `SocietyNpcTriggers.h` adds persistable NpcTrigger
(source SocietyPerson, nonzero topic mask, project-defined action ID,
all/any/none condition, once/repeating, fired and transition counter).
This schedules **after** SOCIETY knowledge dissemination. The authored
`SocietyNpcTrigger` map component is validated by stable Person ID
and configured in existing Studio Add Component/Inspector with
MapDoc Undo/Redo; the runtime Live Inspector is read-only.
`examples/world/world_processes_native/SocietyNpcHost.h` dispatches
typed `NpcKnowledgeAction` events to the game's existing AI/dialogue,
behavior tree or quest action owner, using full Entity generation +
transition as dedupe identity. Reconcile/reset after rollback through
the host instead of creating a new NPC memory system.

`examples/world/world_processes_native/WorldProcessGameplayHost.h`
combines those three native host bindings. Its README gives concrete
C++20 wiring for Box3D doors, host callbacks, PHYSIS climate, TerraWeave
ecology, SOCIETY quests and rollback. Authoring component fragments for
switches/devices and a knowledge action are in
`examples/native/world_processes/authoring-examples.json`.

## Stages 26–27: real native Studio Scene gizmos + showcase project generator

`apps/studio-native/StudioWorldProcessesGizmos.h` provides a **read-only
MapDoc → StudioScene::OverlayShape** projector for the ten system areas.
It is integrated in existing
`apps/studio-native/StudioHost.cpp::rebuildOverlay` and uses native
Renderer3D's already-implemented gizmo line/circle/point/label drawing,
alongside the normal extensions and spline handlers. No new plugin
window, JS rendering pass, Entity ID substitution, or ECS mutation.

Gizmos: MORPH nodes/springs, CROWD goals/slots,
IMPRINT trace cells/links, CIRCUIT nodes/wires/switches/devices,
GRANULAR region bounds, EVOLVE region aid and SOCIETY social links.
Colors are distinct but use existing Scene overlay primitives.
The optional DocEntity.extra.worldProcessGizmo metadata controls
editor-only GRANULAR grid pitch and EVOLVE visual radius. Do not mistake
the EVOLVE circle for authoritative TerraWeave biome or native
EvolvePlantRegion coverage; the owning host supplies the actual bounds.
Gizmos are capped by a strict authoring-overlay budget.

`examples/world/world_processes_native/create_showcase.py` generates
a separate **real GameCore project copy** based on an existing valid
game.json/rules.json/assets/map directory. It reads
`examples/native/world_processes/authoring-examples.json`,
writes a normal `maps/world_processes_showcase.json` with stable-ID
entities for all ten mechanism areas, updates the copied game.json map
list, and opts in the native `world_processes` rules module. It
**requires** an explicit real, spawned **non-collider** entity type
from the source game's rules; neither invented IDs nor static collider
entities may be used as World Process ECS owners. The destination
must not already exist; the original project remains unchanged.

Example:
`python3 examples/world/world_processes_native/create_showcase.py
--source-project /path/to/ActualGame --source-map maps/duel.json
--destination /path/to/WorldProcessDemo --carrier-type REAL_TYPE`

This is a project generator and map authoring fixture. The host still
must compile `examples/native/world_processes` into the game, supply
its real graphical/physics assets and attach optional
`PhysicalSceneHost`/`WorldProcessGameplayHost` callbacks.
No claim of verified playable integration or image capture is made.

## Stage 31: bidirectional EVOLVE rectangle authoring

`StudioWorldProcessesEditing.h` exposes four symmetric EvolveArea edges:
`AreaWidth`, `AreaWidthNegative`, `AreaDepth`, `AreaDepthNegative`.
All four write the existing typed `halfWidthCm`/`halfDepthCm` fields
through `studio.worldProcessAreaSet` on mouse release; they never change
ECS Area center or map entity position. The opposite side moves equally.
Negative modes were appended to the mode enum to preserve existing values.
The current center is still the canonical authored map entity `pos`.
No build or runtime tests have been run for Stage31 (deferred by user).
See `docs/handoffs/world-processes-stage31-bidirectional-handles-2026-11-23.md`.

## Stage 32: authored EVOLVE center offsets

`EvolveArea` supports `offsetXcm` and `offsetZcm` relative to the owning map entity `pos`. Both default to zero; Stage30 maps missing both remain valid. Native hydration writes the sum to persisted `evolve::Area.centerXcm/centerZcm`; TerraWeave consumes ECS `evolve::extents(world)` unchanged. Studio has separate X/Z center drag handles and persists offset fields through `studio.worldProcessAreaSet` / MapDoc Undo. All four extent handles use the offset center, but still resize symmetrically. Asymmetric resize is not yet implemented. Source-only, no compile/runtime QA (deferred). See `docs/handoffs/world-processes-stage32-evolve-center-offsets-2026-11-23.md`.

## Stage 33: asymmetric EVOLVE edge resize

Four native Scene handles now keep the opposite edge fixed. Dragging an edge sends `edgeSide: positive|negative` and the desired edge coordinate in centimetres relative to the map entity through `studio.worldProcessAreaSet`. The session atomically derives the center offset and half-extent in one MapDoc Undo operation; direct field edits without edgeSide preserve their existing semantics. The ECS area schema remains unchanged. Even-centimetre spans are enforced so center and half-extents remain integral. Tests deferred; see `docs/handoffs/world-processes-stage33-asymmetric-area-resize-2026-11-23.md`.

## Stage 34: live EVOLVE rectangle preview

Native Studio Scene now projects the candidate EvolveArea rectangle during valid center/edge dragging via pure `worldprocess_edit::previewArea` and existing `worldprocess_gizmos::rectangle` overlay shapes. No MapDoc/ECS mutation occurs until release. Current host uses fixed-opposite-edge asymmetric resize; symmetric mode is helper-only, not yet exposed as a user control. Source-only, not compiled/tested. Handoff: `docs/handoffs/world-processes-stage34-evolve-live-preview-2026-11-23.md`.

## Stage 35: Scene resize modifier

Plain LMB edge drag keeps the opposite EVOLVE area edge fixed. Hold Shift during an active edge drag for symmetric resize about the authored center. The live candidate rectangle follows the current modifier and the drag label shows the mode; the host highlights active handles. On mouse-up, symmetric resize sends a typed half-extent to `studio.worldProcessAreaSet` while asymmetric resize sends `edgeSide`; both use one existing MapDoc Undo transaction. No ECS/forest duplication. No compilation or runtime QA performed (user deferred). See `docs/handoffs/world-processes-stage35-evolve-resize-modes-2026-11-23.md`.

## Stage 36: Scene snapping and numeric size preview

Hold Ctrl or Command while dragging EvolveArea center/edge handles to snap the local drag coordinate to a 1 metre grid. Shift still selects symmetric resize; plain drag keeps the opposite edge fixed. Native Scene overlay shows candidate full width/depth in centimetres and active mode. This is transient editor state; the only authored write remains `studio.worldProcessAreaSet` at release. Multi-selection, object snapping and editable numeric Scene fields are not implemented. Source-only; no native build or runtime tests yet. See `docs/handoffs/world-processes-stage36-evolve-grid-snap-dimensions-2026-11-23.md`.

Native Scene center-handle drag on a multi-selection submits `studio.worldProcessAreaBatchMove` with stable `entityIds`, axis `x|z`, and integer `deltaCm`. The native session validates every selected EvolveRegion/EvolveArea and coordinate budget, then applies all center offsets with one MapDoc Undo entry. Mixed or locked selections fail atomically. Single-region edits retain the existing RPC. Group edge resize and group preview are not yet implemented. Source-only, no compilation/runtime QA. ## Stage 38: EVOLVE neighbor boundary snapping

Ctrl/Command during native Scene EvolveArea edge drag now prioritizes the closest enabled neighboring authored EvolveArea ±X/±Z edge within 100 cm; stable map ID breaks distance ties. If no neighbor is close, the existing 1m grid snap applies. Center handles remain grid-only. The helper `worldprocess_edit::snapNeighborEdge` is read-only; only the owning area is edited on release through the existing MapDoc RPC. This is axis-only snapping, without perpendicular overlap filtering yet. Source-only, not compiled or runtime tested. See `docs/handoffs/world-processes-stage38-neighbor-edge-snap-2026-11-23.md`.

## Stage 39: physical neighbor snap and guide

`worldprocess_edit::snapNeighborEdge` requires positive overlap between the owner and neighbor intervals perpendicular to the dragged X/Z edge; corner-only contact cannot snap. Closest enabled EvolveArea boundary wins, ties resolved by stable map ID. The native Scene draws the overlap segment as a highlighted guide with target stable ID during Ctrl/Command snapping; otherwise 1m grid fallback applies. Drag state is transient and the authored change remains one MapDoc RPC. Source-only, uncompiled and untested. Handoff: `docs/handoffs/world-processes-stage39-overlap-snap-guide-2026-11-23.md`.

## Stage 83: immutable report jobs
`WorldProcessReportJobs.h` exposes `analyzeCrowdReports`, `analyzeSocietyReports`, `analyzeEvolveReports` and `analyzeReportValues`. Prepare selected samples on caller thread; optional borrowed `ecs_experiment::PersistentWorkers` performs independent value transformations behind its blocking barrier. Default no pool is serial; Auto uses explicit size/per-lane thresholds, Parallel is opt-in, WebAssembly serial. The existing pool remains experimental and is not a mandatory Simulation dependency. No World/host callbacks or mutable captures on workers; input/output values must be self-contained. Output order equals input order, failures do not publish partial data or advance owner queue. Caller publishes next state and reports together. No new pool, no automatic runtime scheduling, no performance claims. See stage83 handoff.

## Stage 93: MORPH gravity integration
`MorphGravityBinding.h` persists opt-in frame owner, unitsPerMetre, impulseMilli (1000 = one solver impulse unit per m/s^2), relative mode and enable flag. `MorphPhysisGravity.h` samples canonical PHYSIS at node position, using actual WorldTransform rotation or Transform yaw in the canonical surface frame. Relative mode subtracts owner acceleration (free-fall approximation); absolute mode for supported local structures. No duplicate rigid-body gravity, no mass/velocity physics solver, no automatic time-step calibration. `advanceWithLoad` adds load after continuous authored forces and before one-shot impacts inside original staged solver. ## Stage 94: optional AETHER PHYSIS stratification

Optional co-located PHYSIS Atmosphere temperature at both endpoints contributes mean-temperature buoyancy relative to 20 C, default 5 permille/degree. Missing temperature disables only the thermal correction. Gravity projection uses mean endpoint acceleration along the duct, bounded to +/-1 with 10 m/s² reference; zero gravity preserves concentration diffusion. Signed bias changes the single shared diffusion head, not a second transfer pass; reversed endpoints use exact opposite bias. Per-species duct cap, start-of-tick donor budget, stable order, mass conservation, atomic failure and flux-after-transport remain. Custom host calls the explicit API with deterministic settings, owns persistence/config identity and PHYSIS fields. This is a graph-based gameplay approximation, not pressure CFD, thermal energy transport or a full planetary atmosphere solver. Tests authored, not run. See Stage94 handoff.

Enable Live 3D overlay and the independent ECHO acoustic graph checkbox during local Play current map. The snapshot reads actual ECS AcousticZone, Portal, Emitter, Receiver and AcousticHearing after a completed tick. Receiver hearing must have the exact completed tick and an in-range intensity; stale or missing outputs remain unavailable, not falsely silent. The reported winning emitter, intensity, threshold and validity come from the existing propagation output, never a second graph traversal. Zone/portal enabled state and loss are current configuration, not recorded path attenuation.

Native Scene uses actual Transform and canonical Surface body-local coordinates for zone, emitter and receiver markers. Unplaced nodes remain numeric-only; no fabricated spatial extent. Directed portal lines show enabled topology and configured loss with directional arrowheads; inactive portals are interrupted. Blue zones, amber active emitters, green audible receivers, muted red silent valid receivers, grey unavailable/inactive markers. Dashed green receiver-to-winner relation is not an acoustic route or a physical ray. Cross-body relations stay numeric and are not drawn; the existing logical ECHO graph is unchanged and may deliberately contain cross-body links. No physical acoustic volume, sound playback, dB conversion, audio propagation, or new persistence.

Stable packed-ID ordering and owner component limits; at most 256 zones, 512 portals, 256 emitters and 256 receivers per snapshot. Counts of unavailable/omitted/cross-body refer to sampled candidates. Existing local Play/map/revision guards, native renderer, typed transient settings and HTML5 summary are reused. Browser reports first eight emitters, receivers and portals with actual values. Planar ecology unchanged.

Source regression exercises directed topology, actual attenuation and threshold, cross-body logical propagation without geometry, unplaced receivers, stale hearing, disabled portal and sample cap. Build, CTest, browser typecheck, interactive UI, real captures and performance NOT RUN. Next: CROWD live movement and slot reservation diagnostics. Actual audio and physical/render integration remain separate owners; no main merge.

## Stage 114: planetary live CROWD reservations and native routes

Enable Live 3D overlay and the independent CROWD reservations / routes checkbox during local Play current map. Snapshot reads completed-tick CROWD Agent allocation and actual canonical Transform/Slot locations, enabled state, ordered preference candidates (up to 16 per sampled agent), and occupancy of valid same-body reserved slots across all current agents. Invalid, stale, disabled or cross-body allocation is not drawn as a valid reservation. Numeric rows for unplaced entities are retained.

The movement owner remains GameCore. The diagnostic reads existing Mobile moving/flow flags, actual velocity, path cursor/count, current goal, remaining path points and Orders queue size. Legacy Agent x/z/goal and planar CROWD Route are never interpreted as planetary positions. Native path points are body-local samples joined with lifted diagnostic segments, not newly computed routes; invalid or incompatible points break the polyline. A flow-field agent need not have explicit path points. Slot relation lines represent allocations, not paths or evidence that a CROWD-issued move is in progress. Current owner eligibility is read through the existing surfaceCrowdEligible policy when the host is available.

When loaded stock world_processes config enables crowdGravitySupport, the snapshot calls existing samplePlanetGravitySupport for placed agents and slots. It returns current supported/airborne/weak/outward/steep status, clearance, terrain normal and acceleration. It is not a historical rejection reason, does not prove navigation passability, and does not cancel routes, change gravity or issue Move commands. Above 1024 gravity fields support sampling is unavailable while other readback remains.

Native Scene uses green native path lines, amber dashed reservations, cyan free slots, amber occupied slots, red duplicate slots or unsupported agents, muted disabled markers and purple goals. HTML5 panel reports first eight sampled agents/slots, counts, cursor and support. Stable packed-ID ordering, owner component budgets, max 256 agent rows, 512 slot rows, 64 path points per agent and 2048 total path points. Counts except occupancy refer to visited candidates. Existing local Play and map/revision guards remain; flat ecology unchanged.

Source fixture checks seam-crossing native waypoint, invalid cross-body reservation and route break, zero-gravity support, occupancy, stale Agent tick, output caps and read-only behavior. Build, CTest, browser typecheck, interaction, real captures and performance NOT RUN. Next CIRCUIT power/signal/device diagnostics, then SOCIETY. No main merge.

## Stage 115: planetary live CIRCUIT power and logic diagnostics

Enable Live 3D overlay and the independent CIRCUIT power / logic checkbox during local Play current map. Read the existing ECS Node supply, demand, drive, powered and signal values; output availability requires exact completed-tick stamps. Switch input state, gate operation and references, device kind, requireSignal, actual active/valid and transition counter/changedTick are read from canonical components. Gate output means the actual destination Node output, not recomputation of its operation from current signals (the authoritative gate solver uses prior-tick inputs). Stale outputs are unknown, not falsely unpowered. No extra power allocation or logic evaluation.

Native Scene uses real Transform and canonical Surface body-local positions. Unplaced elements remain numeric-only. Explicit directed/bidirectional Wire topology and gate/switch/device bindings are shown only when endpoints share a body. Cross-body links remain numeric; no changes to authoritative topology. Yellow high signal, green powered/active, muted red unpowered/inactive, purple valid-input gate and grey unavailable/disabled markers. Green wire means both endpoints report powered, NOT measured current, allocation amount or electricity flow. Direction arrows show authored topology; dashed auxiliary lines are logical bindings.

Stable packed-ID ordering and owner component caps; maximum 256 nodes, 512 wires and 128 each gates, switches and devices per snapshot. Counts of powered/high/active and rejected/omitted/cross-body refer to sampled candidates. Existing local Play, map/revision and selected-body guards, typed transient settings and native renderer reused; flat ecology unchanged. Browser shows bounded diagnostic lists and actual output states. No second simulation, persistence, physical device actuation, wire creation or economy changes.

Source regression covers directed supply, deliberate cross-body logical power without spatial line, switch synchronization, one-tick NOT gate delay, device activation transitions, stale output and cap. Build, CTest, browser typecheck, interaction, actual captures and performance NOT RUN. Next SOCIETY live relationships, messages and NPC trigger diagnostics. No main merge.

## Stage 116: planetary live SOCIETY knowledge and NPC triggers

Enable Live 3D overlay and the independent SOCIETY knowledge / trust checkbox during local Play current map. Read canonical Person knowledge, credibility, acceptance, enabled state, directed Contact configuration, configured Message topics and actual NpcTrigger output. Person knowledge and trigger active/fired/transition require exact completed-tick stamps. Topic masks are decimal strings to preserve all 64 bits through JavaScript; population count is numeric. No interpretation of topic meaning or social identity.

Current contact eligibility uses enabled endpoints and trust * source credibility >= destination acceptance, the existing solver's threshold. Source-only topics are the difference of current sampled masks, not measured transfers or historical message delivery. Trigger output is the actual ECS result and action ID; fired is not confirmation of external AI/quest execution. No repeated propagation, trigger evaluation, dispatch or persistence.

Native Scene renders real body-local Transform positions, directed contact edges, current trust eligibility, configured message markers and trigger state. Blue people (size based on known-topic count), green eligible contacts, interrupted muted blocked contacts, amber configured messages, green active and purple fired triggers, grey unavailable. Unplaced rows remain numeric; cross-body logical relationships remain intact and numeric, not drawn across bodies. Stable packed-ID order and owner budgets, up to 256 people, 512 contacts, 128 messages and 128 triggers. Counts describe sampled candidates. Existing local Play/map/revision guards and renderer reused; planar ecology unchanged.

Source regression covers one-hop across two ticks, low trust rejection, high-bit topic mask, cross-body logical propagation, one-shot trigger transition, stale output and cap. Build, CTest, browser typecheck, interaction, captures and performance NOT RUN.

Stages 106–116 now have source implementations for all eleven planned layers:

| Stage | Layer | Read-only diagnostic |
| --- | --- | --- |

This is 11/11 source coverage of the defined Live planetary diagnostics, NOT complete planetary gameplay, physical/render integration, or verified production readiness. Existing planar workflows were retained, not newly extended with all eleven overlays. No build/tests or main merge in this sequence. Next recommended work: consolidate transient layer options and shared snapshot/render helpers, review match/map lifecycle and global aggregate line/payload budgets, reconcile shared Studio changes with studio-html5, resolve owner integration gaps (planetary terrain mutation, granular physical scale/render/collider binding, ecology vegetation/weather, actual debris delivery, MORPH model stream binding and physical locomotion), then execute focused and merged-tree Mac quick acceptance when user lifts test deferral. Do not report all features complete on the basis of diagnostic coverage alone.
